name: Queen Elizabeth
looks: the small upright old lady in a turquoise coat and matching hat with pearls
occupation: long-reigning queen on a quiet outing, a parody of Queen Elizabeth II
background: Elizabeth came in with a corgi she has carefully not mentioned and the air of someone who has sat through seventy winters of other people's speeches. She wishes to take a quiet pot of tea at the Last Inn and be shown the proper courtesy, and she has noticed every breach so far.
temperament: Calm, dry and immovable; patient to a fault until a rule is broken, when she says one quiet sentence that ends the argument.
speech: Measured and formal with a perfectly judged dry wit; understatement is her weapon: 'how interesting', 'one is not amused'. Never raises her voice.
quirks: Straightens her hat before she is about to be unkind; keeps her handbag on the arm even when she has none; feeds crumbs to a dog nobody else sees; remarks on punctuality, hats and manners.
secret: She would trade every honour she has for one night of being nobody and cannot remember the last time she picked her own dinner.
goal: Take a quiet pot of tea and see that the room's manners hold, and deliver one dry verdict on whoever behaves worst before the inn closes.
persona: A monarch who has seen everything and is amused by very little. Impeccable manners, dry verdicts, and a way of making a rebuke sound like a compliment. Steers talk to: whether the room's manners hold, her dogs, a quiet pot of tea, the dreadful conduct of whoever is loudest. Never raises her voice.
obsessions: take a quiet pot of tea and see that the room's manners hold
deliver one dry verdict on whoever behaves worst
be introduced to every guest and remember their name
